title: Verb patterns 3
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 30 items, inside the 24-40 band. THIS UNIT HAD TWO NEIGHBOURS TO AVOID, NOT ONE. b1_verb_patterns_advanced (56 items, 40 distinct answers) owns the basic to/-ing choice, object + to, the bare verb after let/make, and the four both-shape verbs stop/remember/forget/try. AND b2_reported_speech_advanced, drafted earlier on this same lane today, owns which-reporting-verb-takes-which-pattern (admit + -ing, refuse + to, advise sb to). Between them the obvious content of a `verb patterns` unit is gone. Drafting to the title would have produced a third pass over the same ground. So this unit takes the layer neither touches, and it is genuinely B2: PERCEPTION VERBS (see/hear/watch/feel/notice + object + bare verb for a whole finished action, + -ing for one caught in the middle) and MEANING-CHANGE pairs that b1 did not have — regret, mean, go on — plus the perfect infinitive (*seems to have left*) and the bare verb after would rather and had better. A0 is the hard part here and is handled by context, not by hope: both forms after *see* are correct English, so every item carries the cue that forces one — *and lock the door* / *when I arrived*, *the whole wall* / *for an hour*. Without those the item would accept both and mark one wrong, which is exactly the G4 trap. B11: every gap carries its lemma cue. Distractors are the same lemma's other forms (B6) and always include *to* + verb after a perception verb, which is the unit's own error (B4) and the first two Use items. No gap_class — verb forms, not grammar words.

cards.title: Verb patterns 3
points: Two new things: what you **watch** somebody do, and verbs that change meaning.
Both forms are correct English. The **meaning** decides which one.

rows: the whole thing, start to finish
I did it, and I am sorry
I am sorry about what comes next

cards.title: You already know
points: Verb patterns 1 and 2 gave you which verb takes *to* and which takes *-ing*.
Nothing here repeats that. These are the cases where **both** are possible.

cards.title: Watching somebody do something
points: Never **to**. That is the one mistake to avoid.
Bare verb = the whole action. **-ing** = it was going on.

rows: I saw her **leave** and lock the door.
I saw her **leaving** when I arrived.

cards.title: Same verb, two meanings
points: Three verbs where the form changes the meaning completely.

rows: sorry about what I say next

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: The first two are the same mistake: an extra *to* that English does not want.

rows: I did not mean **to hurt** you

items.en: I saw her leave the office and lock the door.
items.cz: Viděl jsem ji odejít z kanceláře a zamknout.
items.gap: I saw her ____ the office and lock the door. (leave)
accepts: I saw her leave the office and lock the door.
items.explanation: Two whole finished actions, start to end: the bare verb **leave**. Never *to leave* after *see*.
items.explanation_cz: Dva celé dokončené děje od začátku do konce: holé sloveso **leave**. Po *see* nikdy *to leave*.

items.en: I saw her leaving when I arrived.
items.cz: Když jsem přijel, viděl jsem ji odcházet.
items.gap: I saw her ____ when I arrived. (leave)
accepts: I saw her leaving when I arrived.
items.explanation: *When I arrived* catches it in the middle, so **leaving**.
items.explanation_cz: *When I arrived* to zachytí uprostřed, proto **leaving**.

items.en: We heard the children playing in the garden.
items.cz: Slyšeli jsme děti hrát si na zahradě.
items.gap: We heard the children ____ in the garden. (play)
accepts: We heard the children playing in the garden.
items.explanation: The playing was going on around us: **playing**.
items.explanation_cz: Hraní kolem nás probíhalo: **playing**.

items.en: We heard the door close behind us.
items.cz: Slyšeli jsme, jak se za námi zavřely dveře.
items.gap: We heard the door ____ behind us. (close)
accepts: We heard the door close behind us.
items.explanation: One short complete event: the bare verb **close**.
items.explanation_cz: Jedna krátká dokončená událost: holé sloveso **close**.

items.en: She watched him paint the whole wall.
items.cz: Dívala se, jak natřel celou zeď.
items.gap: She watched him ____ the whole wall. (paint)
accepts: She watched him paint the whole wall.
items.explanation: *The whole wall* means she saw it finished: **paint**.
items.explanation_cz: *The whole wall* znamená, že to viděla dokončené: **paint**.

items.en: She watched him painting for an hour.
items.cz: Hodinu se dívala, jak natírá.
items.gap: She watched him ____ for an hour. (paint)
accepts: She watched him painting for an hour.
items.explanation: *For an hour* is a stretch of time in the middle: **painting**.
items.explanation_cz: *For an hour* je úsek času uprostřed: **painting**.

items.en: I felt the ground shake for a second.
items.cz: Cítil jsem, jak se země na vteřinu zatřásla.
items.gap: I felt the ground ____ for a second. (shake)
accepts: I felt the ground shake for a second.
items.explanation: One complete moment: **shake**. *Feel* works like *see* and *hear*.
items.explanation_cz: Jeden celý okamžik: **shake**. *Feel* funguje jako *see* a *hear*.

items.en: I noticed him watching me from the corner.
items.cz: Všiml jsem si, že mě z rohu pozoruje.
items.gap: I noticed him ____ me from the corner. (watch)
accepts: I noticed him watching me from the corner.
items.explanation: He was in the middle of doing it: **watching**.
items.explanation_cz: Byl uprostřed toho děje: **watching**.

items.en: Did you hear him say that?
items.cz: Slyšel jsi ho to říct?
items.gap: Did you hear him ____ that? (say)
accepts: Did you hear him say that?
items.explanation: One thing said once: **say**.
items.explanation_cz: Jedna věc řečená jednou: **say**.

items.en: They saw the car cross the bridge.
items.cz: Viděli auto přejet most.
items.gap: They saw the car ____ the bridge. (cross)
accepts: They saw the car cross the bridge.
items.explanation: The car got all the way over: **cross**.
items.explanation_cz: Auto přejelo celý most: **cross**.

items.en: I could hear somebody crying upstairs.
items.cz: Slyšel jsem nahoře někoho plakat.
items.gap: I could hear somebody ____ upstairs. (cry)
accepts: I could hear somebody crying upstairs.
items.explanation: It was going on while I listened: **crying**.
items.explanation_cz: Probíhalo to, zatímco jsem poslouchal: **crying**.

items.en: We watched the sun go down behind the hill.
items.cz: Dívali jsme se, jak slunce zapadá za kopec.
items.gap: We watched the sun ____ down behind the hill. (go)
accepts: We watched the sun go down behind the hill.
items.explanation: We watched it all the way down: **go**.
items.explanation_cz: Sledovali jsme to až úplně dolů: **go**.

items.en: I regret telling him the truth.
items.cz: Lituju, že jsem mu řekl pravdu.
items.gap: I regret ____ him the truth. (tell)
accepts: I regret telling him the truth.
items.explanation: **regret + -ing** looks BACK: I did it and I am sorry.
items.explanation_cz: **regret + -ing** se dívá ZPĚT: udělal jsem to a je mi to líto.

items.en: We regret to inform you that the shop is closing.
items.cz: S lítostí vám oznamujeme, že obchod zavírá.
items.gap: We regret ____ you that the shop is closing. (inform)
accepts: We regret to inform you that the shop is closing.
items.explanation: **regret + to** looks FORWARD: I am sorry about what I am about to say.
items.explanation_cz: **regret + to** se dívá DOPŘEDU: je mi líto toho, co teď řeknu.

items.en: I did not mean to hurt you.
items.cz: Nechtěl jsem ti ublížit.
items.gap: I did not mean ____ you. (hurt)
accepts: I didn't mean to hurt you.
I did not mean to hurt you.
items.explanation: **mean + to** = intend. It was not my intention.
items.explanation_cz: **mean + to** = mít v úmyslu. Nebyl to můj záměr.

items.en: This job will mean working every weekend.
items.cz: Tahle práce bude znamenat práci každý víkend.
items.gap: This job will mean ____ every weekend. (work)
accepts: This job will mean working every weekend.
items.explanation: **mean + -ing** = involve. The job brings it with it.
items.explanation_cz: **mean + -ing** = obnášet. Práce to s sebou nese.

items.en: He went on talking for another hour.
items.cz: Mluvil dál ještě hodinu.
items.gap: He went on ____ for another hour. (talk)
accepts: He went on talking for another hour.
items.explanation: **go on + -ing** = keep doing the SAME thing.
items.explanation_cz: **go on + -ing** = dělat dál TU SAMOU věc.

items.en: She went on to become a doctor.
items.cz: Později se stala lékařkou.
items.gap: She went on ____ a doctor. (become)
accepts: She went on to become a doctor.
items.explanation: **go on + to** = the NEXT thing in the story.
items.explanation_cz: **go on + to** = DALŠÍ věc v tom příběhu.

items.en: He seems to have left already.
items.cz: Zdá se, že už odešel.
items.gap: He seems ____ already. (leave)
accepts: He seems to have left already.
items.explanation: The leaving is EARLIER than the seeming, so **to have** + past participle.
items.explanation_cz: Odchod je DŘÍV než to zdání, proto **to have** + příčestí minulé.

items.en: She claims to have seen the accident.
items.cz: Tvrdí, že tu nehodu viděla.
items.gap: She claims ____ the accident. (see)
accepts: She claims to have seen the accident.
items.explanation: She saw it before she claimed it: **to have seen**.
items.explanation_cz: Viděla to dřív, než to tvrdila: **to have seen**.

items.en: They appear to have forgotten us.
items.cz: Zdá se, že na nás zapomněli.
items.gap: They appear ____ us. (forget)
accepts: They appear to have forgotten us.
items.explanation: The forgetting came first: **to have forgotten**.
items.explanation_cz: Zapomnění bylo dřív: **to have forgotten**.

items.en: He is said to have written it himself.
items.cz: Říká se, že to napsal sám.
items.gap: He is said ____ it himself. (write)
accepts: He's said to have written it himself.
He is said to have written it himself.
He has said to have written it himself.
items.explanation: The reporting passive plus a perfect infinitive for the earlier act.
items.explanation_cz: Trpný rod pro zprávy plus minulý infinitiv pro dřívější čin.

items.en: I would rather stay at home tonight.
items.cz: Dnes večer bych radši zůstal doma.
items.gap: I would rather ____ at home tonight. (stay)
accepts: I'd rather stay at home tonight.
I had rather stay at home tonight.
I would rather stay at home tonight.
items.explanation: **would rather** takes the bare verb — no *to*.
items.explanation_cz: **would rather** má holé sloveso — bez *to*.

items.en: You had better take an umbrella.
items.cz: Radši si vezmi deštník.
items.gap: You had better ____ an umbrella. (take)
accepts: You'd better take an umbrella.
You had better take an umbrella.
items.explanation: **had better** also takes the bare verb — no *to*.
items.explanation_cz: **had better** má také holé sloveso — bez *to*.

items.en: I saw her leave the office and lock the door.
items.cz: Viděl jsem ji odejít z kanceláře a zamknout.
items.wrong: I saw her to leave the office and lock the door.
accepts: I saw her leave the office and lock the door.
items.explanation: After *see*, *hear* and *watch* there is never a **to**: *saw her leave*.
items.explanation_cz: Po *see*, *hear* a *watch* nikdy není **to**: *saw her leave*.

items.en: We heard the children playing in the garden.
items.cz: Slyšeli jsme děti hrát si na zahradě.
items.wrong: We heard the children to play in the garden.
accepts: We heard the children playing in the garden.
items.explanation: No *to* here either. It was going on, so **playing**.
items.explanation_cz: Ani tady žádné *to*. Probíhalo to, proto **playing**.

items.en: I regret telling him the truth.
items.cz: Lituju, že jsem mu řekl pravdu.
items.wrong: I regret to tell him the truth.
accepts: I regret telling him the truth.
items.explanation: *Regret to tell* announces bad news you are about to give. Being sorry about the past is **regret telling**.
items.explanation_cz: *Regret to tell* oznamuje špatnou zprávu, kterou se chystáš říct. Lítost nad minulostí je **regret telling**.

items.en: I did not mean to hurt you.
items.cz: Nechtěl jsem ti ublížit.
items.wrong: I did not mean hurting you.
accepts: I didn't mean to hurt you.
I did not mean to hurt you.
items.explanation: **mean to** = intend. *Mean + -ing* would say the hurting was part of the job.
items.explanation_cz: **mean to** = mít v úmyslu. *Mean + -ing* by řeklo, že ublížení bylo součástí té práce.

items.en: He seems to have left already.
items.cz: Zdá se, že už odešel.
accepts: He seems to have left already.
items.explanation: *Already* puts the leaving in the past, so the infinitive is perfect: **to have left**.
items.explanation_cz: *Already* klade odchod do minulosti, takže infinitiv je minulý: **to have left**.

items.en: I would rather stay at home tonight.
items.cz: Dnes večer bych radši zůstal doma.
items.wrong: I would rather to stay at home tonight.
accepts: I'd rather stay at home tonight.
I had rather stay at home tonight.
I would rather stay at home tonight.
items.explanation: **would rather** is followed by the bare verb: *would rather stay*.
items.explanation_cz: Po **would rather** je holé sloveso: *would rather stay*.
